title: Stabilizer-rank bound submission
description: A claimed bound on chi(|M>^{ot m}) for one magic-state orbit. Upper bounds carry an explicit decomposition whose terms are given by their stabilizer parametrisation, so a term that is not a stabilizer state cannot be expressed. Lower bounds carry a certificate script that must run and assert.

orbit.description: S Strange, N Norrell, H3 qutrit Hadamard eigenstate, T3 qutrit T-type (face center), qubit_H qubit H-type (edge center), qubit_T qubit Bravyi-Kitaev T-type, T5 ququint T-type (cubic phase x^3 over F_5), qubit_sqrtT the sqrt(T) state (|0> + e^{i pi/8}|1>)/sqrt 2, CS the two-qubit controlled-S magic state CS|++> = (|00> + |01> + |10> + i|11>)/2 (width 2: m copies live on 2m qubits). Family tracks, where m is the qubit count rather than a number of copies: cat, the magic cat state |cat_m> = (|T>^m + |T_perp>^m)/sqrt 2 of Qassim, Pashayan, and Gosset

m.description: number of copies; capped by the verification budget (a 2^10-entry qubit witness verifies in seconds, a 3^10-entry qutrit one would not). For a multi-qubit orbit m counts copies of the orbit state, so m copies of CS occupy 2m qubits and validate_bounds.py caps CS at m <= 4

witness.description: required for an upper bound to earn the verified tier

x0.description: coset representative, length n, the number of qudits the m copies occupy: m for a single-qudit orbit, 2m for CS

W.description: k rows of length n spanning the flat; must be injective

Q.description: quadratic phase form, read upper-triangular and mod p; the phase is w_p^Q(y) for odd p and (-1)^Q(y) for qubits

l.description: linear phase, length k; the phase is w_p^(l.y) for odd p and i^(l.y) for qubits, with l read mod 4 so that every qubit stabilizer state is expressible

coeffs.description: exact sympy expressions, e.g. '3/4 + sqrt(3)*I/4'; no floats

lean.description: required for the lean tier; the module must build and the named theorem must be the bound as stated

theorem.description: name of the theorem inside that module

certificate.description: required for a lower bound to earn the reproduced tier; with `attested` a passing script earns attested, and with `exact` it earns verified

script.description: path relative to the repository root

exact.description: true when the whole argument is exact, including how candidates were enumerated, so that no floating-point margin stands anywhere under the bound; declared by the submitter and checked at review, and it lifts a passing certificate from reproduced to verified. A numerical search followed by an exact rejection does not qualify

budget_s.description: wall-clock seconds the script may run under the verifier, default 900. Declare more only when the search has already been restated as tightly as you can; the value is shown on the board next to the tier and in the ledger, and 3600 is a hard cap

attested.description: declares that the argument is exact and machine-checked but rests on an offline enumeration too large for any certificate budget, whose outputs are stored in the repository. The certificate then checks coverage and hashes of every stored batch, re-decides stored exceptions exactly, and re-runs a subset of batches from scratch; a passing script earns the attested tier, between cited and reproduced. Mutually exclusive with `exact: true`, and requires provenance.compute

batches.description: path, relative to the repository root, of a JSON manifest listing every batch of the enumeration: a list (or an object with a `batches` list) of entries {"id", "params", "output", "sha256"}, where `output` is the batch's stored result file relative to the repository root and `sha256` its hex digest. The verifier requires every output to exist with the stated hash before the script runs

recomputed.description: how many batches the certificate re-runs from scratch and compares bit for bit against the stored output, chosen deterministically from a seed the script prints on a line `seed: <value>`; at most the number of batches in the manifest

compute_hours.description: CPU core-hours the offline enumeration took

note.description: what the completeness of the bound rests on that the certificate does not re-run: the stored batch outputs, the committed runner that regenerates them, and how a reader would re-run the whole enumeration

not.$comment: attested and exact: true are mutually exclusive; the enumeration behind an attested bound is not re-run, so the pipeline did not confirm the whole argument

reference.description: where the bound comes from, e.g. 'arXiv:2605.28586' or 'stabrank PR #16'

method.description: how it was obtained, in one line

date.description: when the bound first appeared: the arXiv v1 date for a literature value, otherwise the date of the work

github.description: GitHub handles, without the @; binds the entry to its authors

compute.description: what the search that produced this bound consumed, aggregated by the site into the discovery ledger. Report what was spent finding the bound, across every run including the failed ones, not what the verifier spends checking it

cpu_hours.description: CPU core-hours over every run that led to the bound

wall_clock_hours.description: elapsed time from the first run to the bound

runs.description: independent search runs, successful or not

hardware.description: machine the search ran on, e.g. 'Apple M3 Max, 14 cores' or 'AWS p5.48xlarge'

llm.description: LLM usage during the search, one entry per model

model.description: model identifier as the provider names it, e.g. 'claude-fable-5-1'

role.description: what the model did: 'drove the search', 'wrote the certificate', 'proposed the ansatz'

cost_usd.description: total spend in US dollars, if known
